thread.title: The grand-plus iPhone is the new normal – this is no place for paupers

author: Pumpkinajn
title: The grand-plus iPhone is the new normal – this is no place for paupers
text: — AAPL Tree (@AAPLTree) September 12, 2018 Analysis So. The £1,000 iPhone X was not an aberration – Apple wants it to be the new normal. A grand is the new "mid-range".Yesterday Apple discontinued its budget iPhone SE and unveiled new models costing £1,500. Since relatively few people switch between platforms, Apple's growth relies in part from making more money from people who already have an iPhone. Phones - Margins - Peripherals - AirPods - Watch That doesn't just mean more phones with a higher margins – but selling peripherals like AirPods and Watch, and upselling Apple services. The latter now generates almost £10bn a quarter, growing a third year-on-year, which offsets stagnating hardware unit sales*. We didn't hear about Apple's much-anticipated Netflix rival service yesterday, but the new fourth-generation Watch impressed. Thanks largely to Apple's chip division, Watch 4 demonstrates a staggering technology lead on rivals.What had been billed as the "Chinese iPhone", the 6.1-inch iPhone XR, is more of a surprise than the revamped X, now bifurcated into large and larger ("Max") models. The XR is dual SIM – although one is an eSIM slot. The "Chinese" label led some to believe it would be aggressively priced, but really it's similarly priced to the regular 4.7-inch iPhone 8 – where Apple believes the sweet spot will be. It starts at £749 (64GB), £799 (128GB) or £899 (256GB). Owners - Models - XR - Display - Upgrade Some owners of older models will revel in the XR's larger display as a natural upgrade. If you don't wear spectacles, Face ID can be a great convenience. Yet look at the comparison with Android rivals. Incredibly, the XR still has a sub-HD display. At 828 x 1,792 pixels its density is identical to the 750 x 1,334 iPhone 8 at 326ppi.And there are missing features.
